I have to give a slight nod to the Boston version as better. It's important to recognize that the 10/14 version is a rather uniquely sprawling landscape, with jagged peaks and valleys (including that explosive ending). But the Boston version is cleaner, tighter, and features a beautiful MIDI flute solo by Jerry.

communityVoices.quote: This show is such a bright shining light in a sea of darkness that defined the last year or two of the Grateful Dead.
this was my 5th show, and by far the best I ever saw...the 5 star rating is relative in this case, as I feel it is indeed the 'last great show' and that has a lot to do with it.
You can hear him giving not only his all but something more.

whyThisShow: This is a broadly canonical show from the final years, included on the official 30 Trips Around the Sun box set, and community reviewers consistently point to it as the peak of 1994. One reviewer called it "the best of '94" and noted that "a great show was not a regular occurrence in '94-'95. In fact, it was rare". Another framed it as "the last TRULY magical night that the boys had before the passing of St.Jerome". One New York partisan who set out to prefer the 10/14 MSG version of Scarlet>Fire conceded that "the Boston version is cleaner, tighter, and features a beautiful MIDI flute solo by Jerry". The first set draws particular attention: one listener wrote that "by any measure, any era, that first set smokes". The one note of complexity is the show's place in a difficult era — the reverence here is partly inseparable from the scarcity of nights this good in the surrounding months.
listenFor: The Scarlet>Fire is the centerpiece and the thing most reviewers name first. One detail worth seeking out: at around 11:25 into the Scarlet track, "Jerry starts doing this little MIDI flute thing, and right as Jerry starts to get cooking on it, Phil immediately starts RIPPING into the Fire bass line and Jerry INSTANTLY takes that little riff and weaves it into a variation on the Fire rythum". One listener called that moment "absolutely PRICELESS" and noted the exchange "only lasts from around 11:25 to 12:15, but its absolutely PRICELESS". So Many Roads also gets a call-out, with one reviewer describing it simply as "exquisite". Stella Blue closes the second set, and one reviewer heard Jerry "goes all out ad-libbing many additional repeatings" and that "as he cries you can hear right down into the very substance of all that he was". The soundboard recording quality draws consistent praise: one listener noted "very good balance between all the instruments. You can easily pick out any instrument in the mix".
context: Boston Garden, October 1, 1994 — final-years era, Vince Welnick on keys. This was among the last shows ever played at the old Boston Garden before the building closed, a fact one reviewer speculated may have sharpened the band's focus: "Perhaps he was aware that this would be the last music ever played in that building". The recording is a soundboard (gd94-10-01.sbd.ashley-bertha.14869.sbeok.shnf) and was officially released as part of the 30 Trips Around the Sun box set. The fall 1994 tour is often cited as a relative bright spot after a difficult summer, and one reviewer noted it "adds credence to the theory that the Dead (and Jerry in particular) were surprisingly coherent in Fall '94".
funFact: One reviewer drew a direct comparison to Cornell, noting the Phil-to-Jerry handoff in Scarlet was a move "ala Cornell".
headline: Boston Garden's last October, Jerry wide awake.
